title: The Silicon Trap
rationale: The episode covers US-China semiconductor competition with the SMIC fab (Beat 3) as the geographic and emotional center. The dominant cultural register is Chinese-state — China's response to US export controls is the episode's most distinctive content. Episode color emphasis is chinese-state to coordinate the Remotion charts (export-control timeline, chip-shortage data, supply-chain map) with the constructivist Chinese-coded illustrations (SMIC fab interior with chinese_propaganda typography, the trap-encirclement atmospheric backdrop). Per VIS-11, the constructivist illustration style stays constant; the palette emphasis varies to fit the cultural context. Default treatment is standard (warm umber default for present-day reconstructions); the trap-metaphor backdrop uses standard with realism: flat for atmospheric backdrop monumentalism. The episode's named conceptual product 'The Silicon Trap' is the recurring visual motif, evolving from simple net diagram in Beat 1 to fully-closed encirclement in Beat 4.

visualMotif.name: The Silicon Trap
visualMotif.description: An interlocking industrial trap formed by factory complexes connected through tangled cable bundles and pipe networks. Begins as a simple net diagram in Beat 1; the network tangles progressively as each beat reveals another constraint; closes fully in Beat 4 as the bifurcation argument lands. The motif's evolution is the episode's emotional spine.
evolutionStates: Beat 1 — simple net diagram, open structure, figures inside but not yet aware of the encirclement
Beat 3 — partial closure, cable tangles tightening, figures performing 34-pass lithography under increasing constraint
Beat 4 — full encirclement, the trap closes around all participants (not just the named adversary), low monumentalist angle
Beat 5 — the trap as personal stakes, your car has 3000 chips inside the closed structure
